source_text.body:
Build a competitor intelligence tool for evidence search
The author tested an agent on competitor research and built a tool to automate evidence search and assessment, noting mistakes in source weighting, deduplication and unsupported certainty.
·
Sep 1, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The builder said they created Vallience as a competitor intelligence tool to automate evidence search and assessment. In practice, the hard part was not finding information but calibrating how the AI evaluated it: they had to keep tweaking how it weighted company claims versus third-party reviews, removed duplicate findings, and avoided overstating conclusions beyond the evidence.
How it went
It worked well enough to automate evidence search and assessment, but the builder said mis-weighted sources, weak deduplication, and unwarranted certainty were persistent errors. They were still refining the system.
Worth knowing
The main catch was calibration time: the builder said it took a long time to tune and is still being adjusted.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Build me a small tool that researches [competitor name or list] on [question, e.g. pricing, features, recent launches] by searching [sources or search terms] and collecting evidence with source links. It should remove duplicate sources, weight sources by reliability (primary sources over blog posts and rumors), and label each claim as confirmed, likely, or unsupported rather than stating everything with certainty. Finish by running it on [one competitor] and showing me the report so I can check it.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/AIAgentsInAction/comments/1w6vghd/could_an_ai_agent_actually_handle_a_workflow_for
